concept.name: Semantic Caching for LLMs

relationships.description: Connects Semantic Caching for LLMs to llm prompt engineering in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Semantic LLM caching intercepts natural-language prompts, embeds them into dense vectors (e.g., 1536-dim via text-embedding-3-small), and performs an Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) lookup in a vector store like Redis or Qdrant. When cosine similarity clears a strict threshold (typically 0.93–0.96), the system returns a cached completion in 20–45 ms instead of paying 1.5–6 seconds and $0.01–$0.05 per frontier model inference.
spark.keyTakeaway: Pair an L1 exact-hash cache with an L2 vector ANN cache gated by tenant metadata filters and high cosine thresholds to cut LLM latency by 90%+ without leaking cross-user context.

concept.whyItMatters: Production LLM applications fail economically and interactively when every paraphrased question ('How do I reset MFA?' vs 'Where can I reconfigure two-factor auth?') triggers a full autoregressive decode. Frontier models cost $2.50–$15.00 per million output tokens and exhibit 1.5–8.0 second end-to-end latencies. In high-volume support, RAG, and coding assistants where 25–45% of traffic is semantically redundant, semantic caching eliminates redundant GPU compute, absorbs traffic spikes without hitting provider RPM/TPM rate limits, and stabilizes p95 response times.
whenToUse: High-frequency, read-heavy Q&A, documentation search, or customer support bots where users phrase identical intents in dozens of ways.
Deterministic or low-temperature (T <= 0.2) workloads where a verified canonical answer remains valid across multiple users.
Cost-constrained pipelines calling expensive reasoning or long-context models (e.g., 32k+ input tokens) with repetitive system prompts.
whenNotToUse: Personalized, stateful, or real-time queries ('What is my current account balance?' or 'Summarize emails from the last 10 minutes') where answers depend on mutable user state.
Creative writing, brainstorming, or high-temperature (T >= 0.7) generation where users explicitly expect novel, non-repetitive outputs.
Code refactoring or data-extraction prompts with subtle negation, numeric, or entity differences ('delete rows > 100' vs 'delete rows < 100') unless guarded by a verifier.
keyPoints: Two-tier lookup beats vector-only: check an L1 SHA-256 exact-match hash (after whitespace/case normalization) in <2 ms before paying ~15–25 ms for an embedding API call and HNSW vector search.

Cosine similarity is blind to negation and swapped entities: 'enable TLS 1.3' and 'disable TLS 1.3' often score >0.94 in bi-encoder embeddings, requiring keyword/entity checks or a fast cross-encoder reranker.
Metadata pre-filtering is mandatory for security: tenant_id, RBAC role, model_version, and prompt_template_hash must be filtered inside the vector index before scoring neighbors.
Cache only the final grounded response alongside its citation IDs and TTL—if underlying RAG documents update, invalidate linked cache keys via document-ID reverse indexes.
Embedding model upgrades invalidate the entire vector space: always namespace cache keys by embedding_model_id (e.g., te3s_v1) to prevent silent similarity drift.

examples.title: Enterprise SaaS Helpdesk Copilot
examples.scenario: A B2B support portal handles 180k daily queries across 4,000 tenant organizations using GPT-4o over a 12k-token product manual, averaging 3.4 s latency and $2,400/day in token spend.
examples.outcome: Adding an L1 Redis exact cache plus an L2 Redis HNSW semantic cache (text-embedding-3-small, cosine >= 0.94, pre-filtered by plan_tier and locale) achieved a 38% hit rate, cutting p95 latency on hits from 3.4 s to 38 ms and saving ~$910/day.

examples.title: Internal SQL-to-Analytics Assistant
examples.scenario: Analysts repeatedly ask variations of weekly revenue and churn questions against a warehouse schema, causing Snowflake and LLM gateway rate-limit (HTTP 429) errors every Monday morning.
examples.outcome: Caching the generated SQL + explanation keyed by semantic intent + schema_version_hash with a 6-hour TTL absorbed 52% of Monday morning burst traffic while still executing fresh SQL against live warehouse tables.

tradeOffs.pro: Lower thresholds (0.88–0.91) boost hit rates by 15–25 percentage points and maximize token savings.
tradeOffs.con: False-positive cache hits return off-topic or dangerously inverted answers on edge-case phrasing.

tradeOffs.factor: Local ONNX embedder vs hosted embedding API
tradeOffs.pro: In-process ONNX models (e.g., BGE-small-en-v1.5) embed in 5–12 ms with zero external network hops or per-token fees.
tradeOffs.con: Consumes app-tier CPU/RAM and locks you into managing model weights and tokenizer parity.

tradeOffs.pro: A lightweight cross-encoder (e.g., ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) catches negation and entity mismatches that bi-encoders miss.
tradeOffs.con: Adds 20–60 ms of CPU/GPU inference latency to every candidate hit and increases serving complexity.

failureModes.name: False-Positive Semantic Collision
failureModes.description: Two prompts share high lexical overlap but opposite intent (e.g., 'Allow port 443 in AWS SG' vs 'Block port 443 in AWS SG'), scoring 0.95 cosine similarity and serving destructive instructions.
failureModes.mitigation: Run a fast entity/negation diff check (comparing extracted numbers, flags, and negation tokens) or a cross-encoder gate before accepting any L2 hit below 0.98.

failureModes.name: Cross-Tenant Context Leakage
failureModes.description: A shared vector index returns Tenant A's cached summary (containing proprietary names or pricing) to Tenant B because their prompt phrasing was identical.
failureModes.mitigation: Enforce mandatory pre-filtering on tenant_id and permission_scope in the vector query (never post-filter top-K results) and segregate sensitive endpoints to exact-match or no-cache.

failureModes.name: Stale RAG Answer Persistence
failureModes.description: A policy or pricing document is updated in the knowledge base, but the semantic cache continues serving yesterday's outdated LLM completion until TTL expiry.
failureModes.mitigation: Store source_doc_ids[] in each cache entry's metadata and trigger targeted cache eviction whenever a source document is re-indexed.

failureModes.name: Embedding Dimension / Model Mismatch
failureModes.description: A deployment switches from OpenAI ada-002 to text-embedding-3-small without flushing or namespacing the index, causing silent zero-hits or corrupted distance comparisons.
failureModes.mitigation: Include embedding_model and dimension count in the Redis/Qdrant collection name and reject queries with mismatched vector metadata.

commonMistakes: Hashing or embedding the entire 10k-token system prompt + conversation history instead of isolating the normalized user intent and context fingerprint.
Using post-filtering on vector search results (fetch top-5, then filter by tenant_id), which yields zero hits when all top-5 belong to other tenants.
Setting a uniform 0.85 cosine threshold across all domains without measuring precision/recall on a golden evaluation set of near-miss pairs.
Forgetting to exclude streaming/non-deterministic tool-calling turns that depend on live timestamps or external API side effects.
Caching unvalidated or hallucinated LLM outputs (e.g., low-confidence or error-fallback responses) and amplifying a single bad generation across thousands of users.

sections.content:
## Caching meaning in vector space instead of exact bytes

Traditional HTTP and Redis caches rely on exact key equality: change a single comma or synonym and `SHA256(prompt)` misses. Semantic LLM caching replaces exact byte matching with geometric proximity in an embedding space. Incoming prompts are mapped to unit-normalized vectors (e.g., 1536 floats), and an Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) index such as HNSW locates the closest previously answered prompt. If the cosine similarity exceeds a calibrated threshold (commonly 0.93–0.96) and all security/context filters match, the gateway short-circuits LLM inference and streams the cached completion back to the client.

## Tracing a request through an L1/L2 semantic gateway

1. **Normalize & L1 Check (1–2 ms):** The gateway strips extra whitespace, extracts `tenant_id`, `model`, and `locale`, and computes `SHA256(normalized_prompt + scope_key)`. An exact hit in Redis returns immediately.
2. **Embed Intent (10–25 ms):** On L1 miss, the gateway embeds only the canonical user query (not the static system prompt) using `text-embedding-3-small` or a local ONNX `bge-small` model.
3. **Filtered HNSW Search (5–15 ms):** The gateway queries Qdrant/Redis HNSW with `filter: {tenant_id == 'acme', prompt_ver == 'v4'}` for `top_k = 3` by cosine similarity.
4. **Guardrail Gate (1–40 ms):** If `score >= 0.94`, a lightweight verifier confirms matching entities, numbers, and polarity (e.g., `>=` vs `<`).
5. **Hit or Async Write-Back:** On pass, return cached tokens with `X-Cache: SEMANTIC-HIT`. On miss, invoke the upstream LLM, stream the response to the user, and asynchronously upsert the `(vector, response, source_doc_ids, ttl)` record.

sections.content:
## Why 0.85 fails and how to tune similarity gates

General-purpose bi-encoders compress syntax and semantics into a single vector, which means structurally similar sentences with opposite meanings ('HTTP 502 on /checkout' vs 'HTTP 504 on /checkout') routinely score 0.91–0.94. Instead of guessing a magic cutoff, collect 500–1,000 production query pairs, label true paraphrases vs near-miss collisions, and plot precision-recall curves per intent category. High-risk categories (billing, IAM policies, SQL generation) typically require `>= 0.96` plus regex entity matching, whereas general FAQ queries tolerate `0.92–0.94`.

## Choosing the right semantic caching backend

| Backend / Pattern | Lookup Latency (p95) | Pre-Filtering Support | Best Fit | Key Limitation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Redis Stack (RediSearch HNSW)** | 5–15 ms | Native hybrid tag + numeric + vector | Unified L1 exact + L2 vector in one cluster | RAM-bound cost at >10M 1536d vectors |
| **Qdrant (HNSW + Payload Index)** | 8–20 ms | Filterable HNSW graph with mmap | Multi-tenant SaaS with complex RBAC | Separate service from L1 string cache |
| **pgvector (HNSW in PostgreSQL)** | 15–45 ms | Full SQL `WHERE` joins & transactions | Transactional RAG apps already on Postgres | Slower under high write concurrency; iterative scan tuning needed |
| **GPTCache / Proxy Middleware** | 20–60 ms | Depends on backing store | Rapid prototyping in Python services | Adds proxy hop and extra serialization overhead |

## Where semantic caches break in production

1. **Negation & Operator Inversion:** 'Show users who *did* pay' vs 'Show users who *did not* pay' can collide in cosine space. Mitigate with a cross-encoder or AST/keyword diff on operators and negation words.
2. **Multi-Turn Context Blindness:** Caching only the last user turn ('How much does it cost?') without the prior turn ('Enterprise plan' vs 'Starter plan') returns the wrong product's price. Always embed a standalone rewritten query (via query-condensation) or include conversation state in the scope key.
3. **Cache Poisoning via Low-Quality Outputs:** If a transient tool timeout causes the LLM to reply 'I cannot access that right now', caching that response locks in the outage for every similar query until TTL expires.

## Keeping cached completions fresh without full flushes

Time-based TTL alone is too blunt for knowledge-backed systems: a 24-hour TTL serves stale pricing for a day, while a 5-minute TTL destroys hit rates. Attach `source_doc_ids` and `prompt_template_hash` as indexed metadata on every cached entry. When your ingestion pipeline updates `doc_482` in the knowledge base, run a metadata delete (`DELETE WHERE 'doc_482' IN source_doc_ids`) to evict only affected answers. Combine this with an LRU/LFU eviction policy and `embedding_model_id` collection versioning so schema or model rollouts never require downtime.

## Production readiness checklist

- [ ] **L1 before L2:** Serve exact normalized SHA-256 matches from Redis in <2 ms before calling any embedding model.
- [ ] **Mandatory scope filters:** Pre-filter by `tenant_id`, `role`, `locale`, `model_id`, and `prompt_version` inside the vector query.
- [ ] **Condense multi-turn queries:** Rewrite follow-up questions into self-contained queries before embedding.
- [ ] **Guard against false positives:** Add an entity/number/negation verifier or cross-encoder for scores between 0.92 and 0.97.
- [ ] **Never cache errors or low-confidence answers:** Gate cache writes on HTTP 200, non-empty tool results, and minimum token length.
- [ ] **Track precision, not just hit rate:** Continuously sample 1–2% of semantic hits for shadow LLM evaluation to detect threshold drift.

interviewProblems.title: Semantic Caching for LLMs
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Semantic Caching for LLMs. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Semantic LLM caching intercepts natural-language prompts, embeds them into dense vectors (e.g., 1536-dim via text-embedding-3-small), and performs an Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) lookup in a vector store like Redis or Qdrant. When cosine similarity clears a strict threshold (typically 0.93–0.96), the system returns a cached completion in 20–45 ms instead of paying 1.5–6 seconds and $0.01–$0.05 per frontier model inference.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Vector Cache (HNSW) applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Upstream LLM.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Upstream LLM experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Run a fast entity/negation diff check (comparing extracted numbers, flags, and negation tokens) or a cross-encoder gate before accepting any L2 hit below 0.98.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Pair an L1 exact-hash cache with an L2 vector ANN cache gated by tenant metadata filters and high cosine thresholds to cut LLM latency by 90%+ without leaking cross-user context.
Avoid trap: Hashing or embedding the entire 10k-token system prompt + conversation history instead of isolating the normalized user intent and context fingerprint.
Avoid trap: Using post-filtering on vector search results (fetch top-5, then filter by tenant_id), which yields zero hits when all top-5 belong to other tenants.
When to reach for it: High-frequency, read-heavy Q&A, documentation search, or customer support bots where users phrase identical intents in dozens of ways.
When to reach for it: Deterministic or low-temperature (T <= 0.2) workloads where a verified canonical answer remains valid across multiple users.

putItTogether.title: Putting Semantic Llm Caching Together
putItTogether.summary: Pair an L1 exact-hash cache with an L2 vector ANN cache gated by tenant metadata filters and high cosine thresholds to cut LLM latency by 90%+ without leaking cross-user context.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Semantic Llm Caching before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Adding an L1 Redis exact cache plus an L2 Redis HNSW semantic cache (text-embedding-3-small, cosine >= 0.94, pre-filtered by plan_tier and locale) achieved a 38% hit rate, cutting p95 latency on hits from 3.4 s to 38 ms and saving ~$910/day.
